title: Clinical predictors, species distribution, and machine learning-based risk stratification of invasive candidiasis and in-hospital mortality: a retrospective episode-level cohort analysis
summary: In this 206-episode cohort, invasive candidiasis occurred in 37 episodes (18%); the Random Forest achieved AUROC 0.987 for invasive disease and 0.776 for mortality. The near-perfect invasive-disease discrimination was driven mainly by age and is explicitly described as exploratory. Five-fold stratified cross-validation with imputation applied within folds; no external cohort, patient-level independence or prospective validation. This supports the reported retrospective result only and not clinical deployment.
ai_technology: Four supervised classifiers (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Extra Trees and Logistic Regression) model invasive candidiasis and in-hospital mortality from 24 clinical and microbiological predictors; permutation importance identifies their contribution.
